subject: Discovery recap: migrating off OpenAI/Anthropic - next steps & compatibility checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@orbitalhealth.com>, Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migrating off OpenAI/Anthropic - next steps & compatibility checklist

Hi Lena / Tom -

Great to meet you both today. Thanks for taking the time to walk through Orbital Health's current stack and the migration goals. Below is a short recap from our call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

TL;DR: Orbital wants to move away from proprietary LLM APIs (OpenAI / Anthropic) toward open models hosted on dedicated infrastructure to reduce per-token costs, improve data control, and avoid vendor lock-in. Primary success criteria are parity on prompt output quality (~95% of current responses), sub-200ms median token latency for chat use cases, and <10% additional engineering effort for integration.

1) Pain points you highlighted
- Per-token costs on current OpenAI calls are growing with volume (billing spike during last quarter).
- Audit/compliance concerns: need stricter data residency and KMS control for PHI-adjacent logs.
- Ops complexity: nightly rate limits and fallbacks; unpredictable throttling during peak inference traffic.
- Model compatibility: several internal prompts use Anthropic-style safety instructions and OpenAI-based system messages; you need minimal prompt rewrite.

2) Current stack (from your notes)
- Front-end: React microfrontend that calls backend RL API.
- Backend: Node.js service calling OpenAI text-generation + Anthropic chat endpoints via server-side wrappers.
- Auth: OAuth2 + internal service accounts.
- Observability: Datadog traces + custom latency dashboards.

3) Success criteria (what you’ll measure)
- Output quality: >=95% fidelity vs. existing API outputs on our 500-prompt eval set.
- Latency: median token latency <200ms on dedicated capacity during p95 traffic.
- Cost: target <=40% of current per-token spend in steady state.
- Deployment/ops: private VPC deployment with KMS/HSM integration and standard audit logs.

4) Compatibility/technical requirements you listed
- Minimal prompt surface changes (support for system+user+assistant roles).
- Function calling / tool invocation support (JSON structured outputs).
- Streaming responses for long generations.
- Embeddings parity for semantic search indexes.
- Rollback capability to OpenAI/Anthropic endpoints during rollout windows.

5) Model shortlist (initial candidates we discussed)
- Llama 3 / 70B quantized variants (for chat parity)
- Mistral 7B/Trident for lower-latency tasks
- Falcon-180B v2 distilled variants (if you need higher instruction-following fidelity)

6) Proposed next steps (action items)
- Redwood: send migration one-pager, proposed migration plan, and security questionnaire responses (attached). Due: Wed 3/11 - Owner: Marissa.
- Orbital: share the 500-prompt eval set and a sample of production traffic (anonymized). Due: Mon 3/15 - Owner: Lena.
- Schedule a tech deep-dive with Aditya (inference lead) and Dev (solutions engineer) to validate kernel/quantization approach and latency targets. Propose Wed 3/17 10:00am PT or Thu 3/18 2:00pm PT.

If that aligns with your notes, I’ll kick off the eval env provisioning and get the NDA/attachment links out.

Thanks again - looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: redwood_migration_one_pager.pdf, proposed_migration_plan.xlsx, security_questionnaire-responses.pdf
From: Lena Ortiz <lena@orbitalhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migrating off OpenAI/Anthropic - next steps & compatibility checklist

Hi Marissa -

Thanks for the thorough recap - this looks right to me. A couple of clarifications/questions from our side:

- Eval set: we can share the 500 prompts but need to scrub any PHI. Will deliver by 3/15.
- Streaming: critical for our longer assist flows (document summarization). Can Redwood support chunked streaming and partial commit semantics (we rely on partial output for UI updates)?
- Fallbacks: during rollout we want automatic fallback to OpenAI with a flag to test rollout traffic. Is that supported without code-level prompt changes?

Tom - tag you: are the proposed deep-dive times good? We prefer Wed 3/17 10:00am PT.

Lena
Head of Data Products | Orbital Health
lena@orbitalhealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena@orbitalhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@orbitalhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migrating off OpenAI/Anthropic - next steps & compatibility checklist

Thanks, Lena - great questions. Quick answers below, we’ll cover details in the deep-dive: 

- Streaming: Yes - Redwood supports chunked streaming and partial output semantics; we'll demo the client-side integration in the tech deep-dive.
- Fallbacks: Supported via routing policies. You can route certain traffic percentages to OpenAI endpoints during canary windows without changing prompt formats - it’s handled at the runtime/router layer.

Aditya / Dev: can you confirm availability for Wed 3/17 10:00am PT for the deep-dive?

I’ll send calendar invites and upload the attachments to the Drive link.

Best,
Marissa
